judged_text: removeMember/addMembers reload via findMembers at the unchanged offset, and findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, ...) against the possibly stale pre-remove user_count. Deleting the last member of a page leaves offset equal to the old user_count, so the reload returns an empty page while earlier members exist (admin must click previous to see anyone); any mid-page removal shifts subsequent members so one row is skipped from the displayed page.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#removeMember` and `#addMembers`, the success callback just calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`/`user_count` first (models/group.js). But `findMembers()` computes the request offset using the *current* (possibly stale) `user_count`: `var ... offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));` and then sends that `offset` to `/groups/:name/members.json`. If the client offset is at the end (e.g., `offset == old user_count`—which can happen via the new pagination action `next` that does `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), a removal that reduces total members can leave `offset` past the new end and `findMembers()` will request an empty page even though earlier members exist. This is directly supported by the diff’s logic and is user-visible broken behavior.
